content:
Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year is rumored to be centered around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three biggest feature differences—excluding price—that could influence your decision on whether to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth highlighting because it's also the most critical distinction.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic form factor that the iPhone has used for years. The screen size and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. The design is completely different—the outer display is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner display resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro remains the strongest

Apple has always packed its most advanced and innovative camera technology into the Pro models. This year will be no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer largely the same camera features as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Reports suggest the iPhone Ultra's main lens, ultra-wide lens, and front-facing lens will match the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens remains exclusive to the Pro, and is rumored to receive an upgrade this year.

Performance: Both feature the A20 Pro chip, but with different materials

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are both expected to run on the same A20 Pro chip at their core. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance may vary slightly.

The iPhone 18 Pro will continue the all-aluminum unibody design of the iPhone 17 Pro, along with a vapor chamber for thermal management. These two changes boosted the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one source has mentioned this so far. Due to the material differences, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may deliver slightly lower performance in direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
